title: Brothers across tribes
hookLine: each Meccan migrant is paired as a brother with a Medinan helper, who shares his home

cards: Arriving in a new city with nothing: that was the situation of the Muslims who followed the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Mecca.
They had left houses, businesses, savings, sometimes family, because staying had become impossible. They didn't know the streets. Some were traders, landing in a town of date groves.
Now the other side. A family in Medina, with a house, a grove, children. One day someone knocks, and they're told: this man is your brother now.
Not as a figure of speech. A brother. Today: the Ansar.

teach.b: The people who left Mecca are called the Muhajirun, the emigrants. The people of Medina who took them in are called the Ansar, the helpers.
The word comes from nasr, help, support, and it became a title of honor they carried for the rest of their lives. The Prophet paired them up, one emigrant with one helper, as brothers.
For a time, early on, these brothers even inherited from each other, until later verses returned inheritance to family. Sahih al-Bukhari tells one pairing in detail.
Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from Mecca, was made brother to Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi', from Medina. Sa'd said: I'm the richest of the Ansar.
I'll split my wealth with you, half and half. Abd ar-Rahman answered: may God bless you in your family and your wealth.
Just show me where the market is. He went, traded, and before long was on his feet. One brother gave everything.
The other took only what he needed.

The Qur'an praises the Ansar in Surah al-Hashr: they love those who came to them, they feel no envy for what the newcomers are given, and they prefer others over themselves even when they themselves are poor.
And remember who the Ansar were: two tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj, who had fought each other for years.
Now they were brothers to each other, and to strangers. Look back over this week: tie the camel, then trust; the Living who holds everything up; light upon light; the Patient who waits.
Then the story again: lift a stone, build plainly, and now, open the house.

how: Muslims remember the Ansar and Muhajirun as models of hospitality and brotherhood, and some communities today pair newcomers, converts or refugees with established families in the same spirit.

ansar comes from a word for help
nasr: help, support. it became their title of honor.

games.q: you're Abd ar-Rahman. you've arrived with nothing. your new brother offers you half his wealth. what do you say?
o: may God bless you. show me the market.
games.why: he blessed Sa'd and asked for the market. one gave everything; the other took only what he needed.

practice: Think of someone who's recently arrived in your world: a new coworker, a neighbor who just moved in, a kid who's new at school, someone new to your mosque, your gym or your city.
Picture them, and what they might be missing, a name, a recommendation, a meal, a map, and one thing you could share. Then sit with what it's like to be on either side of that knock at the door.

wordCard.voice: Ansar. The helpers: the people of Medina who took in the emigrants from Mecca and made them brothers. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the helpers. from nasr, help and support.

carryVoice: Your line: brothers by choice. Half of everything offered, and only the way to the market taken. A week done, see you tomorrow.
